ActorBindingRetiredEvent.description: An operator authorized replacing this binding with a fresh conversation.
ActorBindingRetiredEvent.title: ActorBindingRetiredEvent

ActorIndex.description: Every actor a run's record names, which is every trace it can open.
ActorIndex.title: ActorIndex

ActorRecord.description:
What one actor needs to be reattached after a park.

The digest is recorded here rather than pushed into the runtime because
only this side knows both halves of the comparison. A provider that
restores a resumed thread's tools from its own metadata never says what
it restored, so the answerable question is whether *we* expect the same
schema now that we expected before the park.
ActorRecord.title: ActorRecord

ActorRef.description:
Which actor something belongs to.

A round is part of the identity because the same worker on round two is a
different actor: it holds a different session, and a reader tracing a
decision needs to know which attempt they are looking at.

Here rather than with the record it attributes, because addressing an
actor is not the journal's business alone: the mailbox routes mail by the
same identity, and the two disagreeing about what names an actor is what
makes a redirect reach nobody.

``kind`` is an open string. The consumer names its own roles and validates
them at its own boundary — a closed set here would be every consumer's set
at once, and adding a role to one would mean editing the layer underneath
all of them.
ActorRef.title: ActorRef

AnswerSettledEvent.description: A question took its answer, from whichever door supplied it.
AnswerSettledEvent.title: AnswerSettledEvent

AnswerSubmission.description: Answers submitted from the browser, for any subset of the questions.

answers.description: One value per question being answered now
answers.title: Answers

AnswerSubmission.title: AnswerSubmission

BaseRefreshedEvent.description:
A lease made from here starts from the branch as it stands now.

A run pinned to the commit it was created at cannot see a fix made to
unblock it, and its workers reason about code that has already been
replaced — reaching careful conclusions that contradict decisions the
repository has already taken. Recorded whether it moved or not: a
refresh that could not be made cleanly is the reason the leases beside
it are still where they were.
BaseRefreshedEvent.title: BaseRefreshedEvent

CapturedFileReview.description: The original routed file verdict, bound to its captured input and result.
CapturedFileReview.title: CapturedFileReview

CarriedParent.description: One parent whose commits another parent already contains.
CarriedParent.title: CarriedParent

ConcernAllowance.description:
One edit gate a concern needs, which only a human can grant it.

These gates exist because the decision is a human's. Naming what a plan
needs at plan time moves that decision to where the human is already
deciding, instead of parking the run to ask again for work they just
approved — and a need nobody could have foreseen is asked for mid-lease
and granted to the session that asked.

This enum is the vocabulary's single source of truth: whoever grants a
gate names it from here, the compiled dispatchers honour exactly its
members, and a name outside it is dropped rather than trusted.

Where a lease's current grants live, and why they cannot live here, is
:mod:`lup.policy.grants`: a gate is granted while the session it is
granted to is already running, so unlike an identity it is not something
a launcher can settle in advance.
ConcernAllowance.title: ConcernAllowance

ConcernProgress.description: Atomic persisted status for one concern in the resolver DAG.
ConcernProgress.title: ConcernProgress

ConcernProgressedEvent.description: One concern reached a new status.
ConcernProgressedEvent.title: ConcernProgressedEvent

ConcernStatus.description: Persisted lifecycle of one independently scheduled concern.
ConcernStatus.title: ConcernStatus

ConcernView.description: One concern joined across progress, eligibility, and its outcome.
ConcernView.title: ConcernView

CriteriaCarriedEvent.description:
A human took an acceptance over criteria the reviewer left unmet.

The bar is theirs, so waiving part of it is theirs too, and the waiver
is worth more than the verdict it produced: whoever lands this concern
inherits work that does not meet everything it was admitted against,
and only this says which parts and on whose word.
CriteriaCarriedEvent.title: CriteriaCarriedEvent

EdgeCount.description: How many edges of one kind point at a node — its weight in the log.
EdgeCount.title: EdgeCount

ExportView.description:
Everything a standalone page needs, so it opens with no server behind it.

The graph, every node's detail and the declared kinds, because a page
opened from a file cannot ask for more later — the worked example this
came from was an 18 MB single file for exactly this reason, and a memo
attachment that needed a server would not be one. Stamped with the moment
it was taken, since what it shows is the log as it was then.
ExportView.title: ExportView

ExternalEffectPlan.description:
What an operation does to state or people beyond this machine.

``compensable`` is a claim about the remote *state* — that a normal
follow-up operation restores it — and never about observation. Nothing
un-sends the mail a closed pull request generated, and saying so is what
keeps "compensable" from being read as "free".
ExternalEffectPlan.title: ExternalEffectPlan

ForeignCriteriaEvent.description:
An accepted review credited ids the concern never declared.

Recorded rather than acted on. Every declared criterion was accounted
for, so nothing passed unchecked and the verdict stands; the stray label
is the reviewer's bookkeeping, and turning an acceptance back over it
spent a revision round re-deriving the same verdict until the budget
ran out. Journalled so a reviewer that keeps miscrediting is still
visible to whoever reads the run.
ForeignCriteriaEvent.title: ForeignCriteriaEvent

GraphView.description: The whole log as a graph, with the vocabularies a reader filters by.
GraphView.title: GraphView

IntegrationRecoveredEvent.description: An explicit integration move with its preserved recovery evidence.
IntegrationRecoveredEvent.title: IntegrationRecoveredEvent

JoinAuditEvent.description: The finished tree was re-checked against every parent that built it.
JoinAuditEvent.title: JoinAuditEvent

JoinCompletedEvent.description: One parent was joined, and whether git had to be adjudicated for it.
JoinCompletedEvent.title: JoinCompletedEvent

JoinPlannedEvent.description:
Which parents have to be merged, and which already ride inside one.

Concerns are cut from their dependencies' commits, so the branches stack:
a parent contained in another is already in the tree once that one lands,
and merging it costs a verification and can cost a merger turn to
conclude that nothing happened. Named here rather than left to the skip
inside the loop, so what the run declined to merge is on the record.
JoinPlannedEvent.title: JoinPlannedEvent

JoinRenderedEvent.description:
A join disagreed only in artifacts, and the generator settled it.

Worth recording because it is the difference between a join that cost a
merger turn and one that cost a second: every lease touching a catalog
re-renders both plugin trees, so a conflict there says nothing about the
work and everything about when each branch last generated.
JoinRenderedEvent.title: JoinRenderedEvent

KindInfo.description: One declared kind: its name, what it is for, and what it accepts.
KindInfo.title: KindInfo

KindsView.description: What a project declares: its node kinds and its relations, with their fields.
KindsView.title: KindsView

LeaseDriftEvent.description:
An abandoned concern's tree does not hold the commit last recorded.

Recorded at restore rather than raised. The concern failed, so nothing
in this run reads that tree again — but the work is still on its branch,
and a reader salvaging it wants both commits named.
LeaseDriftEvent.title: LeaseDriftEvent

LeaseRefreshedEvent.description:
What bringing the refreshed base into one lease did, or what stopped it.

The base event above says where the run now starts; it says nothing
about which branches actually took it. An answer reaching stdout alone
is never written down, so a detached run — whose output goes to a
file nobody is watching — keeps no record that three of its leases were
refused. A lease still on the old base is the reason its worker reads
replaced code, which is the failure the refresh exists to prevent.
LeaseRefreshedEvent.title: LeaseRefreshedEvent

MaterialQuestion.description:
A resolver question: the mailbox's shape, plus what the run consults.

The id, the prompt, the answer domain and the two validators over them
are what any door reads, and live on :class:`~lup.coordination.questions.Question`.
Added here is only what the resolver itself consults — which concern the
question belongs to, which edit gates an option would need, and which
lost criteria a re-check is about.

allowances.description: Every edit gate some choice here would need. An option the concern has no grant for is an option whose worker is denied, so naming the gate here is what makes the concern carry it.
allowances.title: Allowances

closed_choices.description: Whether the choices are the complete answer domain. A gate whose reader tests for a literal token closes them; a question whose choices are suggestions leaves them open, so the answer may arrive in the answerer's own words.
closed_choices.title: Closed Choices

criteria.description: The lost criterion ids a re-check question is about, carried as data so an identical standing finding is recognized across occasions instead of re-asked per join.
criteria.title: Criteria

MaterialQuestion.title: MaterialQuestion

MessageCompletedEvent.description:
One whole transcript message completed.

The message is carried rather than reconstructed. Folding loose blocks
back into messages would need contiguous-role grouping, which silently
merges two consecutive assistant messages into one; carrying the whole
message makes the fold exact.
MessageCompletedEvent.title: MessageCompletedEvent

MessageOutstandingEvent.description:
A message still in a member's mailbox as its session is being closed.

Recorded because the sender was told the message was sent, and the mailbox
alone cannot say whether anyone read it. On a park this is a message that
will land at the head of the resumed turn; on a run that ended it is one
that reached nobody, and a redirect nobody read is the failure of an
operation somebody performed to stop something.
MessageOutstandingEvent.title: MessageOutstandingEvent

MessagePostedEvent.description:
A door volunteered something to a member, or a member replied.

An intervention belongs in the record beside what it interrupted. A
reader scrolling one member's trace sees the moment someone redirected
it, in order, against what it was doing — which is the difference between
a trace and an audit filed somewhere else.
MessagePostedEvent.title: MessagePostedEvent

MessageSubmission.description: Something a door is telling an actor. This decides nothing.

in_reply_to.description: Question or message id this answers, if any
in_reply_to.title: In Reply To

redirect.description: Refuse the actor's next tool call and hand it this text as the reason, instead of letting it read alongside what it was doing
redirect.title: Redirect

to_actor.description: Actor label to address. Required to say something; left empty on a redirect it stops every actor that is working
to_actor.title: To Actor

MessageSubmission.title: MessageSubmission

Move.description:
One path an operation renames, and where it lands.

Named rather than paired, because which half of a pair is the source is a
fact a reader has to already know — and the reader who does not is the one
writing the restore.
Move.title: Move

MutationFootprint.description:
Every local path an operation can change, and how exactly it is known.

``exact`` is the whole of what decides which capture covers it. Targets
that resolve statically take a targeted snapshot of exactly those paths;
variables, globs, substitutions, or a directory walk mean the footprint
cannot be enumerated, and the capture widens to every precious writable
root rather than the operation being refused. The wider capture is what
the opacity costs.
MutationFootprint.title: MutationFootprint

NetworkPlan.description:
Where an operation reaches, recorded as evidence rather than policed.

Lup builds no egress proxy, chases no redirects, and polices no DNS: the
boundary's own network posture stands, and this is what the classifier
could see. An operation whose only unusual fact is an unfamiliar
destination settles like any other operation — contained it runs inside,
ambient it follows the profile's declaration.
NetworkPlan.title: NetworkPlan

NodeDetail.description: One node in full: its own fields, its weight, and every edge in and out.
NodeDetail.title: NodeDetail

NodeView.description: One node as a reader meets it: what it is and where it stands right now.
NodeView.title: NodeView

Operation.description:
One immutable native call, normalized, with everything it plans to do.

Immutable because an approval binds to it. A model that could be edited
after a person answered would make "the exact operation was approved" a
claim nothing checks — which is the whole content of exact approval.
Operation.title: Operation

ParkSubmission.description: A door asking every open wait in this run to give up now.

reason.description: Why the run is being parked, recorded for the rerun
reason.title: Reason

ParkSubmission.title: ParkSubmission

PendingQuestionView.description:
One question this run has asked, with whatever answer state it holds.

``offer`` is a value some door proposed that no promoter has taken yet.
Showing it is what makes an offer correctable in the page: a human sees
the pending value and can replace it before it counts.
PendingQuestionView.title: PendingQuestionView

PersistentQuestion.description:
One parked ask, durable, with everything needed to resume it exactly.

The operation is carried whole rather than summarized, because the
requesting agent must not be the thing that reconstructs it: an agent
asked to reissue an approved call is an agent that can reissue a
different one.
PersistentQuestion.title: PersistentQuestion

PhaseChangedEvent.description: The run moved to a new phase.
PhaseChangedEvent.title: PhaseChangedEvent

QuestionAnswer.description: One answer, bound to the question it settles by id alone.
QuestionAnswer.title: QuestionAnswer

QuestionAskedEvent.description: An actor put a material question to the humans.
QuestionAskedEvent.title: QuestionAskedEvent

ReadPlan.description:
Which resources an operation intends to inspect.

Explicit intent, never a syscall trace: Lup does not authorize every read
Git, a compiler, or a package manager performs internally, because doing
so would make a question out of a toolchain reading its own configuration.
What is recorded here is what the operation *named*.

``credential_targets`` is the half that matters. Normal use of a
credential inside the boundary is part of a classified operation; naming
one as the thing to print, copy, or upload is a different operation, and
the two are only distinguishable if the naming is recorded.
ReadPlan.title: ReadPlan

RecheckChangedEvent.description: A recorded finding and a later verdict disagree about lost criteria.
RecheckChangedEvent.title: RecheckChangedEvent

RecheckRepeatedEvent.description:
A re-check reproduced a standing finding already put to the humans.

The same lost-criteria set for the same concern asks once; a later join
that reproduces it is recorded here instead of re-raising an identical
question per join.
RecheckRepeatedEvent.title: RecheckRepeatedEvent

RecheckReusedEvent.description: A resume took these concerns' re-checks from the pass that ran them.
RecheckReusedEvent.title: RecheckReusedEvent

ResolvePhase.description: Persisted resolver phase names in their only valid forward order.
ResolvePhase.title: ResolvePhase

ReviewAnswer.description: A decision bound to the fingerprint the browser displayed.
ReviewAnswer.title: ReviewAnswer

ReviewDecision.description: The recorded answer and the result of notifying its requester.
ReviewDecision.title: ReviewDecision

ReviewDetail.description: Everything the operator reviews before answering.
ReviewDetail.title: ReviewDetail

ReviewError.description: A checkout that could not be read, without hiding its absence.
ReviewError.title: ReviewError

ReviewFile.description: Captured file contents and the corresponding proposed change.
ReviewFile.title: ReviewFile

ReviewHunk.description: A contiguous group of changes with unchanged context around it.
ReviewHunk.title: ReviewHunk

ReviewInbox.description: A complete snapshot of the configured review queues.
ReviewInbox.title: ReviewInbox

ReviewLine.description: One source line, with original terminators and both document positions.
ReviewLine.title: ReviewLine

ReviewNotification.description: Queue acceptance is separate from both approval and recipient delivery.
ReviewNotification.title: ReviewNotification

ReviewResidualEvent.description:
Observations an accepting review recorded beside its verdict.

A residual on a rejected review re-enters the worker's feedback; on an
accepted one nothing else carries it, and real findings would sit unread
in the round records. The journal is where they surface — for the CLI,
the supervisor, and whoever files the follow-up work.
ReviewResidualEvent.title: ReviewResidualEvent

ReviewRoot.description: One operator-selected checkout and its opaque browser address.
ReviewRoot.title: ReviewRoot

ReviewSummary.description: The queue row, with eligibility and a descriptive evidence-based title.
ReviewSummary.title: ReviewSummary

ReviewSuppression.description: A result document's explicit rule exception, located for review.
ReviewSuppression.title: ReviewSuppression

ReviewView.description:
The branch this run built and what mechanically holds about it.

No verdict. Whether twelve merged concerns are jointly right is a
judgement, and the actor that can act on the answer is the agent that
lands the branch — so it is produced from the journal by whoever opens
the run, not persisted here by a reviewer nothing consumed.
ReviewView.title: ReviewView

Row.description: One thing a listing step lists, and what may be done to it.
Row.title: Row

RowAct.description:
One verb offered against one row.

The same shape a terminal menu draws, so a surface cannot offer a verb the
other surface does not have.
RowAct.title: RowAct

RowRequest.description: Which of a row's acts somebody clicked, and the one value it asked for.
RowRequest.title: RowRequest

RunFailedEvent.description: The run reached a terminal failure.
RunFailedEvent.title: RunFailedEvent

RunIndex.description: Every run found under the resolver state root.
RunIndex.title: RunIndex

RunStatus.description: What the run is waiting on, from the operator's view.
RunStatus.title: RunStatus

RunSummary.description: One row of the persisted-run index.
RunSummary.title: RunSummary

ScopeChoice.description: One of the things this wizard can be pointed at.
ScopeChoice.title: ScopeChoice

ScopeRequest.description: A scope somebody asked to make.
ScopeRequest.title: ScopeRequest

StepAnswers.description:
Everything a page submitted for one step.

A list of named answers rather than a bare mapping: what arrives on a
socket is untrusted, and a shape says which keys were expected where a
mapping would take any of them.
StepAnswers.title: StepAnswers

StepField.description: One value a step asks for.
StepField.title: StepField

StepOutcome.description: What running, testing, or undoing a step did.
StepOutcome.title: StepOutcome

StepReply.description: What an act did, and the page as it stands afterwards.
StepReply.title: StepReply

StepStanding.description:
Where a step stands right now.

``done`` and ``offered`` are separate because they answer different
questions and disagree in both directions: a finished step is still
offered when redoing it is how a wrong answer gets fixed, and an unfinished
one is withheld while the step before it is unanswered.
StepStanding.title: StepStanding

StepView.description: One step as the page draws it: the declaration, plus where it stands.
StepView.title: StepView

SupervisorState.description:
Everything one page render needs, in one response.

``phases`` and ``statuses`` are served from the library enums rather
than restated in the page, so adding a phase upstream cannot leave the
frontend silently out of date.
SupervisorState.title: SupervisorState

TurnCompletedEvent.description: A native turn reached a terminal state.
TurnCompletedEvent.title: TurnCompletedEvent

TurnIdentifiers.description: Identities attached to one accepted turn.
TurnIdentifiers.title: TurnIdentifiers

TurnMessage.description: A portable transcript message derived from canonical blocks.

message_id.description: Provider's own message identifier, for correlating replays
message_id.title: Message Id

model.description: Model the provider reports for this message, when it does
model.title: Model

parent_tool_call_id.description: The delegation tool call this message was produced under, when the provider attributes it to one — the only evidence that separates a native subagent's messages from its parent's
parent_tool_call_id.title: Parent Tool Call Id

TurnMessage.title: TurnMessage

TurnNativeActivityBlock.description: Complete provider evidence with no equivalent portable content shape.
TurnNativeActivityBlock.title: TurnNativeActivityBlock

VerificationFailedEvent.description:
What one gate saw at the moment it decided a concern's round.

A run's record held no verification event of any kind: the check ran,
produced a verdict that decided a concern's fate, and left nothing
behind. Journalling it puts what the gate saw beside the turns it
decided about, which is the one place a later session can read it — the
lease worktree the check ran in is usually still held by the run.
VerificationFailedEvent.title: VerificationFailedEvent

WizardView.description: Everything the page needs to draw itself, in one reply.
WizardView.title: WizardView

lup__devtools__dashboard__wizard__Answer.description: One value that came back, against the field that asked for it.
lup__devtools__dashboard__wizard__Answer.title: Answer

lup__policy__relay__Answer.description:
One decision about one question, and who made it.

``note`` is how yes-plus-instructions and no-plus-instructions travel
without a second message. It reaches the agent with the resumption or the
refusal, which is the moment it is worth reading.
lup__policy__relay__Answer.title: Answer
